newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ SEEN READY TO SOFTEN MCI STANCE - ANZ.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ SEEN READY TO SOFTEN MCI STANCE - ANZ.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand is likely to soften in its defence of the "desired" level on The Monetary Conditions Index ANZ Banking Group said on Monday.
Money markets have continued to push an apparent 50-70 tolerance level out to 80-90 and, according to ANZ, the markets expect the RBNZ will sanction a further monetary easing.
In its weekly market focus, the bank said it believes this view to be entirely appropriate given the outlook for inflation and economic growth since the June Monetary Policy Statement.
ANZ said that the less stringent defence of the strict MCI levels is also likely in the future as the Reserve Bank reflects on the events of recent months.
"The source of the problem is the perception created by the MCI of a very rigid trade-off between the exchange rate and the short term interest rates," ANZ said.
So for every significant movement in the TWI markets have been expected to react with a counter-balancing movement in bank bills which ensured the MCI remained steady.

The Reserve Bank has been criticised for its management of monetary policy via this mechanism but in their defence ANZ said this has been a volatile time for the NZ dollar which the MCI has translated into equal volatility in bank bill rates.
Criticism has focused on the 50 basis point margin being too narrow and the 2:1 ratio as inappropiate, as few are exposed to interest rates and exchange rates in such a consistent manner.
And many bank economists see no need for higher interest rates given the soft economy.
ANZ pointed out the Reserve Bank does have some defences against the critics.

Exchange rate movements have been highly unusual and these movements were not included as one of the caveats -- times when it might tolerate greater variation. Also the Reserve Bank has to remain aware of the general impact the dollar and the interest rates will have on the inflation outlook.
ANZ questioned whether financial market stability is being sacrificed in the pursuit of price stability.
It said it expected the following from the September Economic Projections --
* The Reserve Bank will formally ease monetary policy.
* It will emphasise the MCI is a communication tool aimed at keeping monetary conditions broadly appropriate between forecast revisions.
* A statement saying that under certain circumstances they will tolerate wider divergences of actual monetary conditions from the so-called level.
* An increase in the tolerance band and perhaps even the scrapping of
a hard and fast range.
